3.01 General Guidelines for Interactions Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2026

  1. About Interactions

    The National Contact Centers (NCCs) and Public Contact Teams (PCTs) conduct timely, accurate, high-quality interactions with Veterans, Service members, Survivors, dependents, caregivers, and other stakeholders who contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) for benefits information and assistance.

    Interactions may be conducted in-person or via various electronic channels (i.e., telephone, video conference, Ask VA (AVA), chat).

    NCC and PCT employees must:

    • provide complete and accurate information
    • ensure they do not mislead the individual with whom they are interacting by providing information that is not verified in the system of records (subject to ID Protocol requirements in M27-1 I.3.06.)
    • actively listen to properly assist the individual
    • attempt to provide benefit information before referring the individual to general information resources (i.e. VA.gov and the Federal Benefits for Veterans, Dependents, Survivors, and Caregivers benefit book), and
    • ask clarifying questions to determine the correct course of action.

  2. Thanking Individuals for Their Service

    Public Contact Representatives (PCRs) must thank the Veteran or Service member for their service (or the survivors/dependents/family members on behalf of the Veteran/Service member) at any point during the interaction.

  3. Speaking in Absolutes

    There are many variables in the claims and appeal process for VA benefits and services. PCRs must refrain from speaking in absolute terms.

    Examples include (not all inclusive):

    Don't Say Instead Say/Do

    You are/are not eligible for benefits.

    You may file a claim for benefits and VA will make a decision.

    A decision on your claim will be made when…

    Utilize status of claim/appeal scripts.

    VA always pays benefits on the 1st of the month.

    Review the payment for the current month to verify pay date, amount, deductions, etc.

    You will get back pay.

    The effective date of benefits will be determined as part of the decision on your claim. The effective date will determine the amount of any retroactive payment due.

  4. Providing Forms In-Person

    During in-person interactions, when a written request and/or VA form(s) is required to address the issue/concern, PCRs must offer to assist the requestor with completing and submitting the appropriate request/form(s) unless noted otherwise, according to M27-1 I.5.09.

3.02 Opening and Closing Interactions Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2023

  1. Greeting

    To enhance the customer service experience and to ensure the account information is reflected on the screen from the beginning of each phone call, NCC PCRs are required to use one of the following greetings. The greeting used will depend on whether the caller successfully entered information in the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system with Computer Telephony Integration (CTI).

    • Standard Greeting- No information in CTI:
      • VA/Department of Veterans Affairs
      • First name of agent (“This is [name]/[Name} speaking,” etc.)
      • To better/best assist you may I have your/the Veteran's claim/file number or Social Security number (SSN)?
      • Thank you (after receiving claim/file number or SSN)
      • How may I help you?
    • CTI Greeting:
      • VA/Department of Veterans Affairs
      • First name of agent (“This is [name]/[Name} speaking,” etc.)
      • To verify I have the correct record, may I have your/the Veteran's claim/file number or the last four digits of the Social Security number (SSN)?
      • Thank you (after receiving claim/file number or last four of SSN)
      • How may I help you?

    PCT PCRs must appropriately greet the customer, introduce themselves, solicit the Veteran's claim/file number or SSN if not already available, and ask how they may help the customer.

    Notes:

    • Cisco Finesse screens must be visible on PCRs' monitors for quality review purposes.
    • If the PCR's greeting is interrupted, and the caller indicates the question is general in nature, the PCR is not required to request the SSN/claim number and is not required to subsequently thank the caller for providing that information.

  2. Closing

    At the end of an interaction, PCRs are required to ask one of the following closing questions.

    • “Is there anything else I can help you with today?” or
    • “Have I answered all your questions today?” and
    • “Goodbye/Bye”

    Exceptions:

    • For talkative customers, as a method of interaction control, PCRs may instead use a summary statement to close the interaction.
    • For escalated interactions, PCRs are not required to use the standard closing. PCRs should follow guidance in M27-1 I.2. for Escalated Calls/Supervisor Queue, Handling Harassing or Cursing Individual, and/or De-Escalation Techniques.

    Notes:

    • PCRs are required to ask the question once per interaction, when applicable. PCRs are not required to repeat the closing question after any subsequent discussion.
    • “Have a nice/great day” or a similar sentiment must not be used during death-related interactions.

3.03 Systems/Computer Down Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2026

  1. Field User Notification of Systems/Computer Down

    PCRs must provide the mandatory script when instructed via Office of Field Operations (OFO) Business Applications staff email. When systems are available Business Applications staff will send a subsequent email indicating use of the script must cease.

    PCRs may use the outlined additional suggested scripting, along with the alternate closing option, when the mandatory script is in effect.

  2. Systems/Computer Down Scripting

    PCRs must utilize the following scripting as applicable.

    Mandatory Script "VA, this is __________. I apologize for any inconvenience; unfortunately, our computer systems are currently unavailable. I can answer any general questions you may have."
    Suggested Scripts Only one system is down/systems go down during the interaction "I apologize for any inconvenience; unfortunately, the system I need to access to answer your question(s) is currently unavailable."

    Inquirer requests information that requires system access and VA.gov is available

    "With your VA.gov account, you can (insert action/information inquirer has requested) online. The VA.gov website is available at https://www.va.gov/."

    PCRs must provide information on VA.gov and how to obtain an account, if needed.

    Inquirer requests information that requires system access and VA.gov is unavailable

    "Unfortunately, I will need access to your information in order to (insert action/information inquirer has requested) so I am unable to assist you at this time."

    Inquirer requests information on when the system will be back online, and timeframe is known

    "You may call back/return/schedule a new appointment in __________ hours and we will be happy to assist you. Again, I apologize for any inconvenience."

    Inquirer requests information on when the system will be back online, and timeframe is unknown

    "At this time, we do not know when the system will be back online. Again, I apologize for any inconvenience."

    Alternate Closing Options

    If inquirer asks a general question to which the PCR has provided a complete response

    "Do you have any additional general questions I can help you with today?"

    If inquirer indicates they do not have a general question, or the question posed is not general in nature

    "I apologize for the inconvenience. Thank you for contacting us."

3.04 Recording Interactions in CRM/UD-O Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2026

  1. Requirement to Record Interactions

    NCC and PCT employees with access to the Customer Relationship Management Unified Desktop Optimized (CRM/UD-O) system are required to utilize CRM/UD-O to manage and record all interactions.

  2. Interaction Types/Subtypes

    CRM/UD-O users must categorize interactions by selecting the applicable interaction type and subtype from the list of interaction types available.

    In instances where mandatory interaction types and subtypes are required, CRM/UD-O users must use the identified types. PCRs must not edit system notes documenting these mandatory interaction type and subtypes.

    Each unique issue must be categorized by type/subtype for interactions with multiple issues. PCRs do not need to categorize the same issue multiple times when one type/subtype covers multiple actions of the same kind (i.e. multiple letters are requested).

3.05 Sensitive Records Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2026

  1. About Sensitive Records

    Certain records are assigned a level of sensitivity, which restricts access to the records, based on the characteristics of the Veteran, their beneficiaries, or status as an employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

    PCRs must not reference the sensitive level of the individual's record unless directly asked by the individual.

    Important: If the interaction involves an emergency/crisis, PCRs must speak to their coach prior to initiating the referral request typically required by M27-1 I.3.05.b. and c. to determine the appropriate course of action. Standard referrals to the Veteran Crisis Line should be considered, when appropriate.

  2. Sensitive Level 7

    Within the NCCs and PCTs, records with a Sensitive Level 7 must be referred to a PCR with Sensitive 7 system access.

    For interactions requiring access to VA records,

    • NCC PCRs must transfer the individual to the Sensitive 7 queue.
    • PCT PCRs must follow local procedures for referring the individual to another PCT PCR with Sensitive 7 access.

  3. Sensitive Level 8 or Higher

    Within the NCCs and PCTs, records with a Sensitive Level 8 or above must be referred to the Restricted Access Claims Center (RACC). The RACC operates the St. Paul Customer Care Line, 1-888-232-2571, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. CT.

    NCC and PCT PCRs must promote the use of VA.gov for future requests if the individual's issue can be addressed through utilization of VA.gov. PCRs must advise of steps to obtain a VA.gov account, as needed.

    PCRs must follow the guidance in the below table for individuals with a record marked as Sensitive 8 or above who have an inquiry that requires access to their record.

    If… Then…

    the interaction is during St. Paul Customer Care Line operating hours
    • NCC PCRs must provide the St. Paul Customer Care Line telephone number and transfer the call to the care line queue.
    • PCT PCRs must
      • provide the St. Paul Customer Care Line telephone number and transfer the call to the care line queue during telephone interactions, and
      • provide the St. Paul Customer Care Line telephone number and operating hours during in-person or video interactions.

    The interaction is outside St. Paul Customer Care Line operating hours

    NCC and PCT PCRs must

    • provide the St. Paul Customer Care Line telephone number and operating hours,
    • submit a request through the Callback Request SharePoint, and
    • advise someone will call them within 24-48 hours and that call backs are made between 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. CT. The individual may request a specific callback date and time and this information must be entered in the SharePoint entry.

  4. Status of Request for Callback

    PCRs must follow the guidance in the below table for individuals requesting the status of a previously submitted callback request.

    Step Action

    1

    Enter the SSN/file number of the Veteran in the Sensitive 8/9 Callback Status Check Site.

    2

    If the status is:

    • Pending: Advise the callback request is pending and will be completed as quickly as possible. If during St. Paul Customer Care Line operating hours, follow procedures in M27-1 I.3.05.c. for a transfer/referral to the care line queue.
    • Request Complete: Advise the callback was completed. If the individual is requesting to speak with the St. Paul Customer Care Line again, follow transfer/referral procedures in M27-1 I.3.05.c.
    • Unable to Complete: Advise the callback was attempted but was unable to be completed. Follow procedures in M27-1 I.3.05.c. for a transfer/referral to the St. Paul Customer Care Line queue.

    3

    If the individual's issue can be addressed through utilization of VA.gov, promote the use of VA.gov for future requests. Advise of steps to obtain a VA.gov account, as needed.

  5. Pardons and Commutations

    PCRs must advise Veterans seeking assistance in restoring benefits based on Proclamation 10887 to submit:

    • A written statement noting the receipt of a Presidential Pardon and requesting their benefits adjusted accordingly, and
    • A copy of the Certificate of Pardon
      • NOTE: VA Form 21-4138, Statement in Support of Claim, is sufficient to submit a claim to reinstate benefits.

    PCRs must advise the Veteran to submit the required statement and evidence according to Centralized Mail Processing.

    The St. Paul Regional Office Restricted Access Claims Center (RACC) is responsible for processing all cases related to Presidential Pardons and Commutations.

3.06 Identification Protocol (IDP) Back to top
Change Date: February 2, 2026

  1. About Identification Protocol

    First party individuals have an inherent right under the Privacy Act to their own information, or to the information of the person they represent. PCRs must ask required ID Protocol questions to verify that they are speaking to the first party, or an authorized individual, prior to divulging protected information or making changes to a record.

    Protected information includes anything pulled from a living Veteran's/beneficiary's record except the current monthly benefit amount. For a deceased Veteran, protected information is anything pulled from the record except Veteran status, dates of service, branch of service, and location of gravesite in a national cemetery. Records of deceased Veterans may be released to next of kin if disclosures will not be injurious to the physical or mental health of the person on whose behalf the information is sought or cause repugnance or resentment toward the decedent.

  2. ID Protocol Requirements

    All ID Protocol questions must be completely answered directly by the first party inquirer. If the first party provides verbal permission to speak to a third party, the first party must still answer the basic AND enhanced (when applicable) ID Protocol questions.

    Powers of attorney (POA), Veteran Service Officers (VSO), County Veteran Service Officers (CVSO), VA assigned payees (Fiduciary, Guardian, Custodian), and appointed private attorneys or agents are considered first-party inquirers and must be asked the same ID protocol questions as if they were the Veteran or beneficiary.

    Note: ID protocol is not required for

    • VA employees
    • Individuals reporting a first notice of death
    • Claimants submitting an initial intent to file (ITF) when there is no record, and
    • Third party development letter recipients.
      • VA Employees must provide a business need for the requested information and be verified in Outlook.
      • PCRs must ask for enough information to be sure the correct Veteran's record is accessed.
      • PCRs may only discuss the letter received with the third party.

    Responses to ID protocol requirements must be verified in the system of records. After asking required ID protocol questions, PCRs may ask additional questions if they are not comfortable with the responses (see M27-1 I.3.06.c.); however, PCRs may not substitute for any of the required questions if the inquirer is unable to provide the correct response. A note must be left in the system indicating why additional questions were asked.

    The ID Protocol used depends on the type of interaction and requested action.

    Interaction/Action Requested ID Protocol Requirements

    In-Person/Video Interactions

    Valid photo identification, i.e., state-issued driver's license, federal or state identification card

    • If valid photo ID is not available, Telephone Interactions- Standard requirements must be met.
    • If ID proofing is complete without the use of a photo ID, Enhanced Protocol(s) must be met prior to completing the corresponding request/record update.

    Telephone Interactions- Standard
    • Veteran's claim or social security number (SSN)
    • Veteran's full name
    • Veteran's date of birth
    • Veteran's branch of service
    • Caller's full name (not required if caller has already been confirmed as the Veteran)
    • Security question if caller has a valid VA Form 21-0845, Authorization to Release Information to a Third-Party, on record

    Telephone Interactions- CTI
    • Veteran's last four (4) digits of social security number (SSN) or complete claim number
    • Veteran's full name
    • Verify Veteran's entered date of birth matches record
    • Verify Veteran's entered branch of service matches record
      • Entries of “other/not provided” require verbal verification of the branch of service
    • Caller's full name (not required if caller has already been confirmed as the Veteran)
    • Security question if caller has a valid VA Form 21-0845, Authorization to Release Information to a Third-Party, on record

    Spina Bifida Claimants/Beneficiaries
    • Beneficiary's claim or social security number (SSN)
    • Veteran's full name
    • Beneficiary's full name

    For interactions requiring Enhanced ID Protocol (EIDP) to make updates to direct deposit, address, telephone number, and/or email address information (C&P, VRE, and EDU) PCRs must do the following before attempting EIDP:

    Step Action

    1

    Review the record for the “Potential Incident” and “CADD – Written Request Only” fraud flashes.

    • If the “CADD – Written Request Only” flash is on file or the yellow fraud banner appears in the Veterans Benefits Management System (VBMS) Profile screen, proceed to Step 2.
    • If the “Potential Incident” flash is on file, proceed to Step 3.
    • If there are no flashes on record, proceed to Step 4.

    2

    If the “CADD-Written request only” flash is on file or the yellow fraud banner appears in the Veteran's VBMS Profile screen, PCRs must advise the individual to:

    • Submit changes for their direct deposit to use Standard Form 1199a, Direct Deposit Sign-Up Form, and the SSN/Claim number must be in Box C, and Section 3 of the form must be completed by their financial institution.
    • Submit changes for their contact information or cancel direct deposit to use VA Form 20-572, Request for Change of Address/Cancellation of Direct Deposit.
    • Submit the written request in accordance with Centralized Mail Processing to update the payment information, or they can submit the form(s) to a Public Contact Team (PCT)

    Take no further action in this table.

    3

    If the “Potential Incident” flash is on file, PCRs must remain vigilant for an attempt at fraud during the update, proceed to Step 4.

    4

    Review system Notes for updates from the Benefits Delivery Protection & Remediation (BDPR) team and previous potential fraud attempts (e.g. multiple failed attempts over the last several days or weeks) to update information or add a Security PIN.

    • If there are no Notes or updates, proceed to Step 5.
    • If PCRs see information that an individual has attempted/is attempting to make a fraudulent update attempt complete EIDP and ask two additional questions, skip to Step 6.
    • If PCRs see a prior 27-0820 submission in accordance with M27-1 I.3.22.g. procedures for an update pending BDPR review, PCRs must not state the update was sent for review or provide status of the BDPR review. PCRs must advise that the update was submitted and pending. Take no further action in this table.

    5

    Verify if the individual is calling from a telephone number of record.

    • If the individual is calling from a telephone number of record, continue with EIDP, attempt to make the update, and take no further action in this table.
    • If the individual is NOT calling from a telephone number of record, proceed to Step 6.

    6

    Complete procedures in M27-1 I.3.22.g., even if the individual can pass all EIDP.

    Enhanced Protocol questions must be asked and verified in addition to the Standard/CTI requirements to process an addition/removal/change of address, telephone number, email address, direct deposit, or to request copies of documents contained within the eFolder.

    Enhanced Protocol- Change of Address or New Direct Deposit Review the record for flashes - (e.g. “Potential Incident” or “CADD – Written request only”)

    Enhanced Protocol- Change of Direct Deposit
    • Review the record for flashes - (e.g. “Potential Incident” or “CADD – Written request only”)
    • Account number of record
      • If caller is requesting to change or delete a Direct Express Debit® MasterCard® account, the account number of record is not available for verification purposes. All other enhanced requirements must be met to process the requested action.
    • Current payment amount
      • Cents are not required.
      • Individuals have the option to round up or down to the nearest dollar.
      • It is not necessary to ask current payment amount if the individual has not received a first recurring payment.
    • Benefit type (Compensation, Pension, Survivor's Pension, Dependency & Indemnity Compensation (DIC), or Apportionment)
      • It is not necessary to ask benefit type if the caller does not have a pending claim or award running.
    • Veteran's EOD or RAD (MM/YY) for one documented period of service
      • If the individual is a non-Veteran beneficiary, they can verify their own SSN if they are unable to provide the Veteran's EOD or RAD. If the SSN is not available for verification in the system of records, the non-Veteran beneficiary must verify the Veteran's EOD or RAD.
    • Security PIN, if on record
    • Only for Veteran or Survivor beneficiary changes of payment address/new direct deposit

    Enhanced Protocol- Change of Telephone Number or Email Address
    • Review the record for flashes - (e.g. “Potential Incident” or “CADD – Written request only”)
    • Verification of information currently of record (telephone number(s) and/or email address)

  1. Intent to File

    Claimants must file a complete claim, using the prescribed standard form, before a claim will be accepted and established in the system. A complete claim is a completely filled-out standard form. Any communication that is not a complete claim will be considered a request for the proper application form.

    Claims cannot be documented by VA employees. Employees can, however, complete an intent to file (ITF) a claim.

    An individual's statement of his or her “intent to file a claim” must contain sufficient biographical information to identify the individual and they must submit it using one of the following methods:

    • initiation of an electronic claim by the claimant via VA.gov or by a representative via the Accredited Representative Portal (ARP)
    • written on the intent to file form (21-0966, Intent to File a Claim for Compensation and/or Pension, or Survivors Pension, and/or DIC), or
    • orally communicated to VA call center or other public contact personnel.

    If the individual submits the ITF in one of these three ways, it secures the individual's potential effective date and provides the claimant up to one year to complete the appropriate standard claim form and gather evidence to support the claim. Upon receipt of an intent to file, VA will notify the claimant of the appropriate standard claim form required. If a claimant submits a communication that does not meet the requirements of an ITF, VA will still notify the claimant of the standard claim form, if appropriate, but no potential effective date will be secured.

    Notes:

    • PCT employees: If a claimant visits an office in-person and is ready to file the standard claim form for the benefit they are seeking, provide the claimant with the standard form to complete and accept the claim. Advise the claimant on the benefits of electronic filing and the requirements of the Fully Developed Claim process. For claimants who are not yet ready to file the standard claim form, follow intent to file procedures.
    • ITF does not apply to Higher Level Reviews or Appeals to the Board of Veterans' Appeals.
    • ITF does apply to claims filed under 38 U.S.C. 1151. For more information about 1151 benefits see M21-1 VIII.iv.6.
    • Intent to file for benefits means the claimant has stated a desire to apply for benefits. Simply asking about a benefit or eligibility criteria is not enough to establish intent.
    • Authorized third parties appointed by VA Form 21-0845 are not able to submit an ITF on behalf of the claimant. PCRs must advise the authorized third party of the options for the claimant to submit the ITF.
      • Exception: The Authorized third party submits VA Form 21-0972, Alternate Signer Certification, according to M21-1 II.i.2.B.3.c.
    • ITFs can be submitted in CRM/UD-O without the claimant passing Standard Identification Protocol (IDP) as long as PCRs are certain that they are submitting the ITF for the correct record. If not, follow procedures for Veterans and claimants without a record in the below table.

    When a claimant or their representative (fiduciary, appointed Veteran Service Organization (VSO), or VA recognized attorney) expresses the intent to file a claim, PCRs must take the following actions.

    Step Action

    To increase customer service and first interaction resolution, designated Processing Teams are authorized to establish claim End Products (EPs) or contentions, complete information corrections prevented by technical issues, and file documents in correct locations.     Category Requirements

    Discrepant Data

    Discrepant data occurs when there is conflicting information within VA systems. PCRs must initiate referrals to request confirmation of the correct information and an update to the system. Examples of situations where a referral to correct discrepant data is required (not all inclusive):

    • Claim closed, but notification letter not available in the system of records.
    • Claim denied, but evidence/information that may have impacted the decision was available in the mail portal at the time the decision was completed, and the evidence is now located in the eFolder with no EP 930 established.
    • Incorrect requirements provided in correspondence for submitting a claim or appeal action
      • claim submitted via VA electronic claim submission system is cancelled due to generation of an outdated version of the VA Form and claimant advised claim must be submitted on the current version of the VA Form. See M21-1, III.ii.1.C.8.a for additional information on this issue
      • claim decided prior to AMA rollout, claimant advised must follow new appeal process, or
      • claim decided after AMA rollout, claimant advised must follow old appeal process.

    For corrections to name, date of birth, and service information when the discharge document for that period of service is viewable in the eFolder, PCRs must follow procedures in M27-1 I.3.23.

    Priority Claim Status

    Priority claims are carefully monitored for overdue suspense dates and are quickly moved through the claims process by eliminating delays between actions and stages. See M21-1 X.i.1. for information on which claims may receive priority.

    PCRs must initiate referrals for claims identified as priority cases when:

    • evidence was submitted more than ten (10) calendar days ago, it is viewable in the eFolder/Mail Portal, and action has not been taken on it (e.g. file not flashed)
    • the claim level suspense is past due
    • the claim is pending initial development for more than ten (10) calendar days
    • an expedited process is not being followed, or
    • the claim appears ready for an action or the next step of the process, yet it has not occurred.

    Exception: In the instance of a successful warm transfer to the Homeless Veteran Coordinator (HVC), or HVC participation in PCT interaction, PCRs must not initiate a VA Form 27-0820 for the bulleted reasons above.

    Terminal Illness Hardship Claimed

    • Document the caller's statement along with prognosis and if they are treated at a VA Medical Center (VAMC)
    • Advise the caller to submit medical documentation and the doctor's prognosis

    Financial Hardship Claimed

    • PCRs must use the "Hardship: Financial Hardship Claimed" CRM/UD-O quick write:
    • "The [Veteran, authorized third party, etc.] reported they are experiencing extreme financial hardship due to [insert hardship reason], and request that their disability compensation claim [insert claim EP and date] be expedited. They were advised to submit documentation to support the request, if available. Please review to add a Hardship flash."
      • The VAF 27-0820 must include additional information if the claimant indicates they cannot submit documentation, e.g. the hardship is due to a natural disaster.

    PCRs must initiate a referral if there has been no action after thirty (30) calendar days on a previously appropriately submitted VA Form 27-0820 (series).

    Exception: For priority claim referrals, if there has been no action after seven (7) calendar days, PCRs must refer the issue to a DMO for escalation. DMOs must contact the Claim/Appeal Inquiry POC listed in the KM Desk References (in the case of no POC listed, contact the IPC Coach).

    Board of Veterans' Appeals Escalations (Board)

    PCRs are required to initiate referrals in the following situations:

    • A VA Form 10182, Board Appeal (Notice of Disagreement) was received, the item displays as “Complete” in the Packet Status column of the CMP, and the appeal is not established in Caseflow
      • PCRs must review the form for completeness before submitting an escalation (e.g. the issue being appealed is listed/not under review in another lane/not being appeals for a non-C&P business line, etc.).
    • A VA Form 10182 displays as “Processing” in the Packet Status column of CMP for more than ninety (90) calendar days.
      • PCRs must review the form for completeness before submitting an escalation (e.g. the issue being appealed is listed/not under review in another lane/not being appeals for a non-C&P business line, etc.

    • Board decision was completed more than fourteen (14) calendar days ago but is unavailable in VBMS. If an address change was completed during the interaction, PCR must include this information in the referral.

    • Motion (MOT) to the Board for reconsideration/revision/vacate inactivity is available in VBMS with no designation of the appeal as MOT or corresponding diaries/correspondence for more than two (2) calendar months.

3.31 Military Payments Back to top

  1. Military Retired Pay and Other Military Payments

    Military retired pay (MRP) benefits may be paid based on age, length of service, or disability. Federal law (38 U.S.C. 5304(c)) generally prohibits duplication of payments when a Veteran receives MRP. If a military retiree is granted VA compensation, they must tell us which benefit they elect to receive. Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP) allows military retirees to receive both military retired pay and VA compensation. Combat Related Special Compensation (CRSC) is a program that was created for disability and non-disability military retirees with combat-related disabilities.

    Other military payments which were paid in a lump sum upon separation from service require a total withholding of all VA benefits until the lump sum amount has been recouped. These payouts are normally found on the DD-214 and in the Military History tab of UDO. Some military benefits may require partial withholding of VA compensation benefits for a specific time period, or the appropriate amount of the lump sum has been recouped.

    PCRs must answer inquiries about

    • the withholding and payment process
      • eligibility criteria and program information for CRDP and CRSC.
      • recoupment amounts and balances for lump sum military payments, and
      • the difference between a debt and an award adjustment.

    PCRs must refer:

    • Individuals with further inquiries about military retirement benefits to Defense Finance and Accounting Services (DFAS) at 1-800-321-1080.
    • Coast Guard retirees and annuitants to the Coast Guard Pay and Personnel Center at 1-800-772-8724.
    • Individuals to the DEERS Support Office (DSO) at (800) 538-9552 for assistance with updating the Veteran or a dependent's name in DEERS.

  2. Recoupments and Financial Hardship

    When a Veteran asserts the recoupment of a lump sum military payment (i.e. severance or separation pay) is an undue burden based on their current financial situation they can request VA reduce the amount being recouped each month. This request is allowed whether the claim has been decided, and the recoupment is already in place, or if recoupment has only been proposed.

    PCRs are required to advise:

    • about eligibility requirements
      • this is not a request to waive the recoupment and there is no guaranteed withholding amount
      • there is no prescribed form for making the request and to submit the written request for reduction along with VA Form 5655, Financial Status Report.
      • VA will only accept a request from the Veteran, their VA-recognized representative, or fiduciary, and
      • the Veteran will be notified when a decision is made.

    For more information see M21-1, VI.ii.2.

    The term drill pay refers to the monetary benefits a reservist or member of the National Guard receives for performing active or inactive duty training.

3.34 Crisis Interactions Back to top
Change Date: February 2, 2026

  1. Suicidal Individual

    PCRs must recognize the signs of a crisis. An individual may not specifically state they are going to commit suicide. PCRs must be able to analyze and pick up on clues that could indicate the individual is in danger of harming themself or others. Listed below are some phrases that could indicate crisis and require that the PCR ask probing questions to determine if additional action is necessary:

    • I don't want to live anymore.
    • My family would be better off if I was no longer here.
    • I am in too much pain to deal with this anymore.
    • I don't want to go on.
    • I am giving away everything I own since I won't need it anymore.
    • There is no way to solve this problem, I don't have any options.

    For individuals in crisis, PCRs conducting telephone or virtual interactions must take the following actions.

    Step Action

    1

    Evaluate the crisis. Use the NCC Suicide Ready Reference Assessment to determine the individual's risk level. Ask the individual, "Are you thinking of suicide?" or "Are you having suicidal thoughts?"

    • Transfers should not occur for high-risk callers.
    • Callers that are at high risk should not be placed on hold.

    2

    Notify your internal support network. Get assistance by either:

    • using the "emergency" button in CRM-UD/O, or
    • asking another employee to get a supervisor.

    3

    Obtain the individual's location and information, as needed.

    Obtain the following information:

    • individual's name,
    • present location
    • telephone number or the number from which the caller is dialing,
    • alternate phone numbers (if different from the caller's present location), if available, and
    • last four digits of Social Security number.

    4

    Offer crisis resources. For callers, determine if the caller is safe before attempting to transfer to the Veterans Crisis Line (VCL). Never transfer a caller that is in an unsafe situation, or you've assessed as high risk.

    Low risk and caller is safe:

    • Offer to transfer the caller to the Veteran's Crisis Line
    • Provide the caller with the VCL telephone number:
      • 1-800-273-8255, Press 1 or
      • 988, Press 1
    • Attempt to transfer the call to the VCL using the warm transfer number: 833-825-2273
    • When transferring the call, use the following script:

    “This is (PCR's name) with the VBA National Call Center in (your location). I have (name of caller) on the line. Their call back number is XXX-XXX-XXXX. The last four digits of their SSN are XXXX.” (PCR should speak clearly)

    High risk or caller is unsafe:

    • If the caller is unwilling to be transferred or you feel it is unsafe to place the caller on hold, or the caller is high risk, then:
      • do as the caller wants
      • remain on the telephone, and
      • do NOT transfer or place the caller on hold.

    The supervisor should silently monitor the call and seek second-party assistance through a:

    • VA medical facility
    • local counseling psychologist, and/or
    • local emergency services, if necessary.

    5

    Verify the individual's status.

    • Is anyone else there with them?
    • Are they currently receiving medical treatment?
    • What is the name(s) and phone numbers of family, friends or a significant other?

    6

    Support the caller during the crisis. Continue with the interaction until the crisis is managed and under control, and the interaction can be safely terminated.

    7

    Document the interaction using VA Form 27-0820, Report of General Information, and forward the form to the appropriate station of jurisdiction.

    For individuals in crisis, PCRs conducting in-person interactions must take the following actions.

    Step Action

    1

    Evaluate the crisis. Use the NCC Suicide Ready Reference Assessment to determine the individual's risk level. Ask the individual, "Are you thinking of suicide?" or "Are you having suicidal thoughts?"

    • Referrals to VCL should not occur for high-risk callers.

    2

    Notify your internal support network. Get assistance by either:

    • using the "emergency" button in CRM-UD/O, or
    • asking another employee to get a supervisor.

    3

    Obtain the individual's information, as needed.

    Obtain the following information:

    • individual's name,
    • telephone number,
    • alternate phone numbers if available, and
    • last four digits of Social Security number.

    4

    Offer crisis resources.

    Low risk and individual is safe:

    • Offer to contact the VCL
    • Provide the individual with the VCL telephone number:
      • 1-800-273-8255, Press 1 or
      • 988, Press 1
    • Attempt to contact the VCL using the internal number: 833-825-2273
    • When the VCL answers, use the following script:

    “This is (PCR's name) with the VBA Public Contact Team in (your location). I have (name of caller). Their call back number is XXX-XXX-XXXX. The last four digits of their SSN are XXXX.” (PCR should speak clearly)

    High risk or individual is unsafe:

    • If the caller is unwilling to be connected to the VCL or the individual is high risk, then:
      • do as the individual wants, and
      • do NOT contact the VCL with the individual.

    The supervisor should seek second-party assistance through a:

    • VA medical facility
    • local counseling psychologist, and/or
    • local emergency services, if necessary.

    5

    Verify the individual's status.

    • Are they currently receiving medical treatment?
    • What is the name(s) and phone numbers of family, friends or a significant other?

    6

    Support the individual during the crisis. Continue with the interaction until the crisis is managed and under control, and the interaction can be safely terminated.

    7

    Document the interaction using VA Form 27-0820, Report of General Information, and forward the form to the appropriate station of jurisdiction.

  2. Suicidal Crisis Healthcare

    Veterans in acute suicidal crisis can go to any Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) or non-VA health care facility for emergency health care at no cost - including inpatient or crisis residential care for up to thirty (30) days and outpatient care for up to ninety (90) days. Veterans do not need to be enrolled in the VA system to use this benefit.

    If… Then…

    individuals request benefit information

    PCRs must provide that, under this policy, VA will:

    • make appropriate referrals for care following the period of emergency suicide care.
    • determine eligibility for other VA services and benefits.
    • refer eligible individuals for appropriate VA programs and benefits following the period of emergency suicide care.

    individuals request eligibility information

    • former members of the armed forces, including reserve service members, who served more than 100 days under a combat exclusion or in support of a contingency operation either directly or by operating an unmanned aerial vehicle from another location who were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable.
    • former members of the armed forces who were the victim of a physical assault of a sexual nature, a battery of a sexual nature, or sexual harassment while serving in the armed forces.

    individuals have questions PCRs cannot answer,

    PCRs must offer the telephone number and transfer to the Community Care Call Center at 877-881-7618.

    the individual is in crisis,

  3. Gun Lock Initiative

    Gun locks may be distributed by the ROs at outreach events, along with the Brochure for Veterans Means Safety (va.gov), or at the public contact office. Additionally, gun locks may be requested and provided during home visits by field examiners or for specially adapted housing visits. Veterans can also request gun locks at their local VA Medical Center through the Suicide Prevention Coordinator.

    For individuals needing to obtain a gun lock from VA, NCC PCRs must advise the individual how to visit their local PCT or VA Medical Center.

    If, at any time during the interaction, the individual behaves in a manner that indicates he/she may be in crisis, at risk of crisis, or needs assistance with mental health care treatment at the VA Medical Center, the PCR must immediately address these issues.

    The VHA Office of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention has provided the following SharePoint site for PCTs to request additional gun locks, in increments of one hundred (100): New item | Gun Lock Request (sharepoint.com).

  4. Threat to Employees or VA Facilities

    Employee safety is a priority, and workplace violence will not be tolerated. Threats to employees and VA facilities are taken very seriously.

    Upon receipt of a threat, PCRs must

    • immediately notify a supervisor using:
      • the "Emergency" button in CRM/UD-O for NCC and PCT PCRs, or
      • the panic button for PCT PCRs, or
      • instant message (IM) for employees that receive a threat by email/chat/AVA
      • immediately fill out the Physical Threat on Employee or Bomb Threat Checklist online form and send to Management.

    Note: PCT employees conducting in-person interactions must follow local emergency procedures and may activate a panic button if the office is equipped.

    During the interaction, management must

    • assist the PCR in any way possible and begin efforts to notify the affected office's Director's Office as soon as possible. Initial contact of the situation does not need to wait until the conclusion of the interaction.

    After the interaction, management must

    • immediately forward the completed form to the affected office's Director's Office by email (or hand carry if appropriate), and
      • call the affected office's Director's Office, if emailed.

    Note: It is critical that the affected Director's Office is notified of the threat as quickly as possible. Management should attempt to gain the assistance of their own Director's Office to contact another RO or VA Medical Center.

3.35 Natural Disaster Guidance Back to top

  1. Responding to Inquiries About Natural Disaster Assistance

    Natural disasters, i.e., hurricanes, tornadoes, floods, etc., impact Veterans and beneficiaries in many ways. Depending upon the individual's circumstances, PCRs must:

    • categorize the interaction as Type: Natural Disaster, with the applicable Sub-Type.
    • document requests for time limit extensions and reports of missed local hearings or Compensation and Pension Exams on VA Form 27-0820, Report of General Information, and route according to M27-1 I.5.07.
    • follow existing procedures regarding claim expedition for individuals experiencing hardship because of the natural disaster.
    • follow guidance in M27-1 I.3.24 regarding Board of Veterans' Appeals (Board) hearings. Appellants must submit requests for advancement on the docket at the Board in writing.
    • PCRs must make appropriate referrals to other VA business lines, i.e., Education, Home Loan Guaranty, etc.
    • PCRs may utilize guidance found in the Natural Disasters Fact Sheet to assist with responding to additional questions.
    • PCRs must provide information about VA Health Connect to Veterans that are impacted or displaced by a natural disaster to access virtual care services.

3.37 Privacy Act Violations Back to top
Change Date: September 30, 2026

  1. Report of Privacy Act Violation

    When a Veteran/beneficiary/third party reports they received another individual's information (e.g. another individual's letter, sees another Veteran's dependent information on VA.gov, etc.) PCRs must take the following actions:

    Step Action

    1

    Thank the individual for reporting the situation and apologize for the inconvenience.

    2

    For correspondence packages sent from claims processors through Centralized Printing, review the Veterans Benefits Management System (VBMS) Package Manager.

    • Locate the Distribution where the violation occurred.
    • Review the documents in the Distribution to determine if a claims processor added incorrect documents to the package.
      • If yes, meaning there is a document(s) in the package that is for someone other than the intended recipient, note this on the 27-0820, Report of General Information, as indicated below.
      • If no, meaning all documents in the package were for the intended recipient, note this on the 27-0820 as indicated below.

    3

    Complete VA Form 27-0820, Report of General Information, using the “Privacy Act Violation” CRM/UD-O quick write:

    • date of reported incident
    • mailing date and/or receipt date of the correspondence
    • details of incident to include the name of individual(s) whose record or information was affected
    • if information improperly received was a prepared letter, obtain the information of the individual who prepared the correspondence item, if available, for example:
      • first line of information under the heading, “In reply refer to” section
      • identification information provided after the enclosure line in the letter
      • note whether the correspondence was sent through Centralized Printing and whether any incorrect documents were included in the Distribution.
    • the name, address, telephone number, and Social Security number and/or claim number, if appropriate, of the individual reporting the incident
    • the status of the documents
      • if the inquirer has the documents in their possession,
      • if the inquirer has destroyed the documents,
      • if the inquirer has already mailed the documents back to VA, or
      • if the inquirer indicates he/she will return the documents without waiting for contact, instruct him/her to return them to the office shown on the letterhead, to the attention of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)/Privacy Act (PA) Officer.

    Note: If the caller received a CD, the CD must be returned.

    4

    Advise that they will be contacted to discuss retrieval of the documents.

    Note: PCT PCRs must notify the local Privacy Officer if the inquirer brings the documents to the PCT office.

    5

    Route the VA Form 27-0820 via encrypted email to your supervisor or designee for immediate action.

    6

    When the Veteran/beneficiary reports they saw someone listed as a dependent (e.g. on VA.gov or a letter from VA) and they indicate this person is unknown to them and has never been their dependent, PCRs must follow additional guidance in M27-1 I.3.23.h.

  2. Required DMO Actions

    All referred incidents must be appropriately addressed by the supervisor or designee within twenty-four (24) hours. Upon receipt of the report from the PCR, the supervisor must take the following actions.

    Step Action

    1

    Immediately review the VAF 27-0820 to ensure all required information is included on the form.

    Note: When identifying information is unavailable regarding which station or which employee created the letter, supervisors must utilize additional resources to locate this information, including:

    • reviewing award printouts in the eFolder for the name of the authorizer
      • reviewing the life cycle tab in CRM/UD-O for the name of the authorizer
        • reviewing system notes

    2

    After confirming all necessary information is included on the form, send the form as outlined below, via encrypted email marked with high importance (!).

    • If the correspondence item received was in response to a FOIA/PA request that was processed by the Centralized FOIA/PA team, send the completed VA Form 27-0820 to Privacy.VBASTL@VA.gov with subject line “Privacy Act Violation – Immediate Action Required.”
    • If the correspondence item received was sent directly by a regional office (RO) (without the use of Package Manager), send the completed VA Form 27-0820 to the Privacy Officer at the RO that sent the correspondence item with subject line “Privacy Act Violation – Immediate Action Required.”
    • If the correspondence item received was sent via Package Manager, send the completed VA Form 27-0820:
      • to the Privacy Officer at the RO that prepared the package when Package Manager shows incorrect/comingled Veteran information, indicating that the RO user made the mistake. Use subject line “Privacy Act Violation – Immediate Action Required.”
      • to the Package Manager vendor PII drop box when Package Manager shows all the correct and matching information for the claimant in question, indicating that the Centralized Printing vendor made the mistake. Use subject line “Print Vendor PII Violation.”

    3

    For reports routed to the RO, call the appropriate Privacy Officer and advise of the incident and that a completed VA Form 27-0820 has been sent. If unable to reach the Privacy Officer, contact the alternate Privacy Officer. It is not acceptable to leave a voicemail message.
